12: 
13: # Figma to Code Translation
14: 
15: How to read a Figma design as a reference and build the simplest correct structure from it.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: A Figma read, export or MCP pull tells you what the screen should look like and which states it has. It does not tell you which elements to write.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Reading a Figma frame before writing code
28: - Translating auto layout, sizing or absolute layers into CSS
29: - Mapping Figma variables and styles to installed tokens
30: - Running the five-pass check against a rendered build
31: - Reporting a Figma-to-code red flag
32: 
33: ### Core Principle
34: 
35: Figma is a reference for code, never its markup. Never copy the layer tree, absolute coordinates, fixed frame sizes or component property sets 1:1 into code.
36: 
37: ### Boundaries
38: 
39: This file does not own:
40: 
41: - **Element choice.** That decision belongs to [`web-markup-and-css.md`](web-markup-and-css.md), and every value comes from the tokens the app installs.
42: - **Shared principles.** The shared principles are in [`frontend-practice.md`](frontend-practice.md). The web layer names the mechanics each app uses.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. WHY FIGMA COMPONENTS LOOK THE WAY THEY DO
47: 
48: Design teams build one Figma component to serve many use cases without creating a new variant for each. That flexibility costs structure:
49: 
50: - **Boolean properties** that show or hide layers, so one button covers icon-left, icon-right and text-only.
51: - **Instance-swap slots** that accept any icon or nested component.
52: - **Nested auto-layout wrapper frames**, added to control padding, alignment or clipping on the canvas.
53: - **Absolutely positioned layers**, so the component stays resizable in the editor without its parts reflowing.
54: - **Fixed frame widths and text boxes with set sizes**, sized for one artboard, often a 375 px phone frame.
55: - **Variants for states** (hover, pressed, focus, disabled) and sizes, because Figma has no pseudo-classes or props.
56: 
57: That structure serves the canvas and the designer. Code usually needs a simpler, more effective structure: fewer elements, normal flow, states from CSS or props, and values from tokens.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## 3. TRANSLATION TABLE
62: 
63: | Figma construct | Web |
64: |-----------------|-----|
65: | Auto layout, direction | `display: flex` with `flex-direction`, or grid for two axes |
66: | Auto layout spacing between items | `gap` with a spacing token |
67: | Auto layout padding | `padding` with spacing tokens, logical properties |
68: | Hug contents | Intrinsic size: no width set, or `fit-content` |
69: | Fill container | `flex: 1`, or stretch in the parent |
70: | Fixed width or height | `max-width` or a size token, only when the fixed size is intended |
71: | Absolutely positioned layer | Normal flow, a positioned overlay only when the design truly overlays |
72: | Hidden layer or boolean property | Conditional rendering or a prop |
73: | Instance swap | Children or a slot |
74: | State variant: hover, pressed, focus, disabled | `:hover`, `:active`, `:focus-visible`, `:disabled`, ARIA state attributes |
75: | Size variant | One `size` prop mapped to tokens |
76: | Figma variable or style | The token the app's installed package exports |
77: | Layer name | A hint for the element choice, never a class name |
78: | Frame pixel value | A token, or `rem` for type |
79: | Effect: drop shadow, blur | A shadow token |
80: | Icon instance | The app's icon component, or inline SVG with `currentColor` |
81: 
82: A row with no token to map to is a finding to report, not a reason to paste the Figma value.
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 4. WORKFLOW
87: 
88: 1. Read the design context with a read-only Figma transport from the Section 5 tool ladder.
89: 2. Name the component's job, its content and every state, including empty, loading, error and disabled.
90: 3. Look for an existing component and existing tokens in the app before writing anything new.
91: 4. When the frame leaves a value open, or a value is off every token and scale, load [`sk-design-fundamentals`](../../../sk-design/sk-design-fundamentals/SKILL.md) and decide the value there, not here. A frame that maps cleanly to tokens needs no design step.
92: 5. Write the simplest semantic structure that does the job, ignoring the layer tree.
93: 6. Map every value to a token. Report any value that has no token. The value table in this step is Pass 4's variable-to-token table.
94: 7. Check the result with the five-pass check in Section 5.
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: ## 5. THE CHECK
99: 
100: ### Read-Only Inputs
101: 
102: Gather these inputs before comparing the frame with the rendered build:
103: 
104: - The Figma file key and node id.
105: - The authored frame width W, read from the frame and never set. Resizing the frame changes the design and is a write.
106: - The variants and state nodes.
107: - The Figma variables and `node bindings` used by the frame.
108: - The installed token package and its version.
109: - The rendered build.
110: 
111: ### Figma-Side Tool Ladder
112: 
113: Use these read-only transports in order:
114: 
115: 1. The official Figma MCP when it is connected natively in the runtime. This route belongs to the frontend reference. The tools exposed by this runtime are `get_design_context`, `get_screenshot`, `get_metadata` and `get_variable_defs`. Their return shapes belong to the runtime, not this reference. The connected server's own instructions require `create_session` with the file key before any file tool, including read-only tools. They also require loading its `figma-design-to-code` skill before calling `get_design_context`.
116: 2. The Framelink figma manual through Code Mode, only after discovery confirms it is registered. It returns design data and can download referenced images. It does not return variable bindings, so Pass 4 cannot run from Framelink alone.
117: 3. `figma-ds-cli`, which requires Figma Desktop and its daemon. For the Pass 1 frame image, the documented form is `figma-ds-cli export node <nodeId> -o ./out/frame.png -s 1`. Its read-only Pass 4 commands include `node bindings` and `var list`. Its read-only Pass 5 commands include `a11y contrast`, `a11y touch`, `a11y text`, `a11y focus` and `a11y audit`. Confirm exact group flags with the documented help before relying on them.
118: 4. A static export already in the packet, marked as possibly stale.
119: 
120: The official Figma MCP is a native runtime connection. The `mcp-figma` skill documents its own CLI and the separate Framelink Code Mode manual. It does not route or wrap the official MCP.
121: 
122: ### Passes by Figma Transport
123: 
124: | Transport | Pass 1 | Pass 2 | Pass 3a | Pass 3b | Pass 4 | Pass 5 |
125: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
126: | Official Figma MCP (runtime) | `get_screenshot` provides a frame image | `get_design_context` and `get_metadata` identify design context; state capture coverage is `UNKNOWN` | App render check | Changed source check | `get_variable_defs` | `UNKNOWN`: the named runtime tools document no Figma-side accessibility check |
127: | Framelink figma through Code Mode | `UNKNOWN`: referenced image downloads are documented, full-frame screenshot export is not | `UNKNOWN`: variant coverage is not specified | App render check | Changed source check | Not supported alone: Framelink returns no variable bindings | `UNKNOWN` |
128: | `figma-ds-cli` | export node supports a frame image | `UNKNOWN` | App render check | Changed source check | `node bindings` and `var list` | Partial: documented read-only a11y commands support contrast, touch, text, focus and audit checks |
129: | Static packet export | Frame image can be compared, but may be stale | `UNKNOWN` | App render check | Changed source check | `UNKNOWN` | `UNKNOWN` |
130: 
131: Passes 3a and 3b are checked against the rendered application and changed source, not supplied by a Figma transport. `UNKNOWN` means the referenced documentation does not establish support.
132: 
133: `spec --check` measures a built node inside Figma. It does not compare the application render with the frame.
134: 
135: ### Five Passes
136: 
137: | Pass | Evidence source | Pass condition | Fail condition |
138: |---|---|---|---|
139: | 1. Same-width comparison | Web: render at the frame's authored width W at device scale 1 beside the frame image. Compare presence, order, wrapping, alignment and overflow. | Every frame element is present in order, there is no overflow at W, and no fixed width was copied. | An element is missing or extra, wrapping differs, overflow occurs, or a mismatch changes meaning. Pixel difference alone never fails. |
140: | 2. State by state | Every variant plus the empty, loading, error and disabled states named at workflow step 2. Dark mode only where the mode supports it. Motion is not in design unless the frame specifies it. | Each state has a capture and a verdict, and one component with props covers them. A state absent from the design is recorded as not in design. | A state is unrendered, there is one component per variant, or a state contradicts its frame. |
141: | 3a. Render token check | Web: resolved styles from bdg cdp Runtime.evaluate and getComputedStyle. Use the Pass 4 table to map Figma variables to tokens. | Every resolved color, spacing, radius, depth, type and breakpoint value matches an installed token value, or a package lag is reported. | A resolved value is in no installed token. Resolved styles turn var() into their final value, so this pass cannot distinguish a token from a literal of the same value. Pass 3b checks source usage. |
142: | 3b. Source token check | Search changed source files for literal colors, sizes and font values where a token exists. Run the repository's own token checker if it has one. | No literal appears where a token exists, and the repository checker passes when one is available. | A literal appears where a token exists, or the repository checker fails. |
143: | 4. Variable to token | Read each used Figma variable and node binding, then compare with the installed token package and version. Record one row per variable: Figma variable \| Figma value \| installed token \| installed value \| verdict. | Every variable maps to an installed token, or a package lag is reported. An open value goes to sk-design-fundamentals per workflow step 4. | A Figma variable name or value appears in code, or a missing variable is treated as resolved. |
144: | 5. Range and access | Web: widths below and above W across phone, tablet and desktop widths, 200 percent zoom, keyboard-only use, screen reader, and contrast for text and controls against their backgrounds. | Each check has a verdict, and none fails. | An element clips or overlaps, a keyboard trap or unreachable control appears, a name, role or state is missing, or contrast is below the target set by sk-design-fundamentals. When no project target exists, use WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text under [success criterion 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#contrast-minimum), plus 3:1 for user-interface components and graphical objects under [success criterion 1.4.11](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#non-text-contrast). |
145: 
146: Capture mechanics: see [Capture Mechanics on the Web](#capture-mechanics-on-the-web).
147: 
148: ### Capture Mechanics on the Web
149: 
150: Every recipe below ran against a live page with `bdg` 0.6.10. For methods with parameters, use `bdg cdp <Domain.method> --params '<json>'`; `bdg cdp --help` confirms the form.
151: 
152: Open the rendered build in a `bdg` session.
153: 
154: - Set the viewport to the frame's authored width W in CSS pixels with `bdg cdp Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride --params '{"width":<w>,"height":<h>,"deviceScaleFactor":1,"mobile":<bool>}'`.
155: - Set the colour scheme the frame shows before capturing, because a headless browser follows the system setting: `bdg cdp Emulation.setEmulatedMedia --params '{"features":[{"name":"prefers-color-scheme","value":"light"}]}'`.
156: - Capture with `bdg dom screenshot <path>`.
157: - Read resolved styles for Pass 3a with `bdg cdp Runtime.evaluate --params '{"expression":"getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(\"<css>\")).<property>","returnByValue":true}'`. `bdg dom eval` failed with "Session target not found" in the same session, so use `Runtime.evaluate`.
158: - **Pass 2, state by state:**
159:   1. Enable the domains once per session: `bdg cdp DOM.enable`, then `bdg cdp CSS.enable`. `CSS.forcePseudoState` needs the CSS domain enabled.
160:   2. Resolve the document with `bdg cdp DOM.getDocument` and use its `root.nodeId` as `<rootId>`. Resolve the element with `bdg cdp DOM.querySelector --params '{"nodeId":<rootId>,"selector":"<css>"}'` and use the result's `nodeId` as `<id>`.
161:   3. Emulate reduced motion first, `bdg cdp Emulation.setEmulatedMedia --params '{"features":[{"name":"prefers-reduced-motion","value":"reduce"}]}'`. A style read straight after forcing a state otherwise returns a mid-transition value.
162:   4. Force each state with its own call, `bdg cdp CSS.forcePseudoState --params '{"nodeId":<id>,"forcedPseudoClasses":["hover"]}'`, then `["active"]` and `["focus"]`. Force `focus-visible` only when `bdg cdp --describe CSS.forcePseudoState` confirms support. Clear with an empty `forcedPseudoClasses` list before the next state.
163:   5. The disabled state comes from the element's `disabled` attribute, not a forced class.
164:   6. Capture each state with `bdg dom screenshot <path>`, and confirm the capture shows the state.
165:   7. Check dark mode with the same `setEmulatedMedia` method and `{"name":"prefers-color-scheme","value":"dark"}`, only where the project supports dark mode. Reset with `--params '{"features":[]}'`.
166:   8. If CDP cannot run, use real hover, click and keyboard focus. If neither path runs, record `NOT RUN` with the reason.
167: - **Pass 5, range and access:**
168:   1. Test narrow, medium and wide widths below and above W with `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`. Reset with `bdg cdp Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride`.
169:   2. Check 200 percent zoom with `bdg cdp Emulation.setPageScaleFactor --params '{"pageScaleFactor":2}'`, and reset with `1`.
170:   3. Traverse the page with real Tab presses, and record the focus order and any trap.
171:   4. Check names, roles and states with `bdg cdp Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, or with a manual screen-reader pass.
172:   5. Read computed text and background colours with `Runtime.evaluate` as above, then check contrast against the target `sk-design-fundamentals` sets.
173:   6. Record any check that cannot run as `NOT RUN` with the reason.
174: - Use [mcp-aside-devtools](../../../mcp-tooling/mcp-aside-devtools/SKILL.md) as the fallback renderer. Its `aside repl` is Playwright-compatible and can capture screenshots, but it has no CDP-domain parity, so it cannot force states or emulate media. Keep `bdg` for those checks.
175: 
176: See [mcp-chrome-devtools](../../../mcp-tooling/mcp-chrome-devtools/SKILL.md) for documented `bdg` commands.
177: 
178: ### Verdict and Report
179: 
180: The overall result is `PASS` only when every pass passes. Record a pass that cannot run as `NOT RUN` with its reason, and the overall verdict is then `INCOMPLETE`, never `PASS`.
181: 
182: The report names:
183: 
184: - The frame, node id and W.
185: - The installed token package and version, and the tool used for each pass.
186: - Capture paths, the state matrix, the rendered value table and the variable-to-token table.
187: - The lag list and overall verdict.
188: 
189: ---
190: 
191: ## 6. RED FLAGS
192: 
193: Stop and restructure when the code shows any of these:
194: 
195: - Most children are absolutely positioned.
196: - A literal frame width such as `375px` or `width: 375`.
197: - A fixed height on a container that holds text.
198: - Wrapper depth that mirrors the Figma layer panel.
199: - Pixel or hex literals pasted from the inspect panel.
200: - One component per Figma variant instead of one component with props.
201: - Class names copied from layer names, such as `.frame-427` or `.auto-layout-wrapper`.

71: | Absolutely positioned layer | Normal flow, a positioned overlay only when the design truly overlays |
72: | Hidden layer or boolean property | Conditional rendering or a prop |
73: | Instance swap | Children or a slot |
74: | State variant: hover, pressed, focus, disabled | `:hover`, `:active`, `:focus-visible`, `:disabled`, ARIA state attributes |
75: | Size variant | One `size` prop mapped to tokens |
76: | Figma variable or style | The token the app's installed package exports |
77: | Layer name | A hint for the element choice, never a class name |
78: | Frame pixel value | A token, or `rem` for type |
79: | Effect: drop shadow, blur | A shadow token |
80: | Icon instance | The app's icon component, or inline SVG with `currentColor` |
81: 
82: A row with no token to map to is a finding to report, not a reason to paste the Figma value.
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 4. WORKFLOW
87: 
88: 1. Read the design context with a read-only Figma transport from the Section 5 tool ladder.
89: 2. Name the component's job, its content and every state, including empty, loading, error and disabled.
90: 3. Look for an existing component and existing tokens in the app before writing anything new.
91: 4. When the frame leaves a value open, or a value is off every token and scale, load [`sk-design-fundamentals`](../../../sk-design/sk-design-fundamentals/SKILL.md) and decide the value there, not here. A frame that maps cleanly to tokens needs no design step.
92: 5. Write the simplest semantic structure that does the job, ignoring the layer tree.
93: 6. Map every value to a token. Report any value that has no token. The value table in this step is Pass 4's variable-to-token table.
94: 7. Check the result with the five-pass check in Section 5.
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: ## 5. THE CHECK
99: 
100: ### Read-Only Inputs
101: 
102: Gather these inputs before comparing the frame with the rendered build:
103: 
104: - The Figma file key and node id.
105: - The authored frame width W, read from the frame and never set. Resizing the frame changes the design and is a write.
106: - The variants and state nodes.
107: - The Figma variables and `node bindings` used by the frame.
108: - The installed token package and its version.
109: - The rendered build.
110: 
111: ### Figma-Side Tool Ladder
112: 
113: Use these read-only transports in order:
114: 
115: 1. The official Figma MCP when it is connected natively in the runtime. This route belongs to the frontend reference. The tools exposed by this runtime are `get_design_context`, `get_screenshot`, `get_metadata` and `get_variable_defs`. Their return shapes belong to the runtime, not this reference. The connected server's own instructions require `create_session` with the file key before any file tool, including read-only tools. They also require loading its `figma-design-to-code` skill before calling `get_design_context`.
116: 2. The Framelink figma manual through Code Mode, only after discovery confirms it is registered. It returns design data and can download referenced images. It does not return variable bindings, so Pass 4 cannot run from Framelink alone.
117: 3. `figma-ds-cli`, which requires Figma Desktop and its daemon. For the Pass 1 frame image, the documented form is `figma-ds-cli export node <nodeId> -o ./out/frame.png -s 1`. Its read-only Pass 4 commands include `node bindings` and `var list`. Its read-only Pass 5 commands include `a11y contrast`, `a11y touch`, `a11y text`, `a11y focus` and `a11y audit`. Confirm exact group flags with the documented help before relying on them.
118: 4. A static export already in the packet, marked as possibly stale.
119: 
120: The official Figma MCP is a native runtime connection. The `mcp-figma` skill documents its own CLI and the separate Framelink Code Mode manual. It does not route or wrap the official MCP.
121: 
122: ### Passes by Figma Transport
123: 
124: | Transport | Pass 1 | Pass 2 | Pass 3a | Pass 3b | Pass 4 | Pass 5 |
125: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
126: | Official Figma MCP (runtime) | `get_screenshot` provides a frame image | `get_design_context` and `get_metadata` identify design context; state capture coverage is `UNKNOWN` | App render check | Changed source check | `get_variable_defs` | `UNKNOWN`: the named runtime tools document no Figma-side accessibility check |
127: | Framelink figma through Code Mode | `UNKNOWN`: referenced image downloads are documented, full-frame screenshot export is not | `UNKNOWN`: variant coverage is not specified | App render check | Changed source check | Not supported alone: Framelink returns no variable bindings | `UNKNOWN` |
128: | `figma-ds-cli` | export node supports a frame image | `UNKNOWN` | App render check | Changed source check | `node bindings` and `var list` | Partial: documented read-only a11y commands support contrast, touch, text, focus and audit checks |
129: | Static packet export | Frame image can be compared, but may be stale | `UNKNOWN` | App render check | Changed source check | `UNKNOWN` | `UNKNOWN` |
130: 
131: Passes 3a and 3b are checked against the rendered application and changed source, not supplied by a Figma transport. `UNKNOWN` means the referenced documentation does not establish support.
132: 
133: `spec --check` measures a built node inside Figma. It does not compare the application render with the frame.
134: 
135: ### Five Passes
136: 
137: | Pass | Evidence source | Pass condition | Fail condition |
138: |---|---|---|---|
139: | 1. Same-width comparison | Web: render at the frame's authored width W at device scale 1 beside the frame image. Compare presence, order, wrapping, alignment and overflow. | Every frame element is present in order, there is no overflow at W, and no fixed width was copied. | An element is missing or extra, wrapping differs, overflow occurs, or a mismatch changes meaning. Pixel difference alone never fails. |
140: | 2. State by state | Every variant plus the empty, loading, error and disabled states named at workflow step 2. Dark mode only where the mode supports it. Motion is not in design unless the frame specifies it. | Each state has a capture and a verdict, and one component with props covers them. A state absent from the design is recorded as not in design. | A state is unrendered, there is one component per variant, or a state contradicts its frame. |
141: | 3a. Render token check | Web: resolved styles from bdg cdp Runtime.evaluate and getComputedStyle. Use the Pass 4 table to map Figma variables to tokens. | Every resolved color, spacing, radius, depth, type and breakpoint value matches an installed token value, or a package lag is reported. | A resolved value is in no installed token. Resolved styles turn var() into their final value, so this pass cannot distinguish a token from a literal of the same value. Pass 3b checks source usage. |
142: | 3b. Source token check | Search changed source files for literal colors, sizes and font values where a token exists. Run the repository's own token checker if it has one. | No literal appears where a token exists, and the repository checker passes when one is available. | A literal appears where a token exists, or the repository checker fails. |
143: | 4. Variable to token | Read each used Figma variable and node binding, then compare with the installed token package and version. Record one row per variable: Figma variable \| Figma value \| installed token \| installed value \| verdict. | Every variable maps to an installed token, or a package lag is reported. An open value goes to sk-design-fundamentals per workflow step 4. | A Figma variable name or value appears in code, or a missing variable is treated as resolved. |
144: | 5. Range and access | Web: widths below and above W across phone, tablet and desktop widths, 200 percent zoom, keyboard-only use, screen reader, and contrast for text and controls against their backgrounds. | Each check has a verdict, and none fails. | An element clips or overlaps, a keyboard trap or unreachable control appears, a name, role or state is missing, or contrast is below the target set by sk-design-fundamentals. When no project target exists, use WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text under [success criterion 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#contrast-minimum), plus 3:1 for user-interface components and graphical objects under [success criterion 1.4.11](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#non-text-contrast). |
145: 
146: Capture mechanics: see [Capture Mechanics on the Web](#capture-mechanics-on-the-web).
147: 
148: ### Capture Mechanics on the Web
149: 
150: Every recipe below ran against a live page with `bdg` 0.6.10. For methods with parameters, use `bdg cdp <Domain.method> --params '<json>'`; `bdg cdp --help` confirms the form.
151: 
152: Open the rendered build in a `bdg` session.
153: 
154: - Set the viewport to the frame's authored width W in CSS pixels with `bdg cdp Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride --params '{"width":<w>,"height":<h>,"deviceScaleFactor":1,"mobile":<bool>}'`.
155: - Set the colour scheme the frame shows before capturing, because a headless browser follows the system setting: `bdg cdp Emulation.setEmulatedMedia --params '{"features":[{"name":"prefers-color-scheme","value":"light"}]}'`.
156: - Capture with `bdg dom screenshot <path>`.
157: - Read resolved styles for Pass 3a with `bdg cdp Runtime.evaluate --params '{"expression":"getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(\"<css>\")).<property>","returnByValue":true}'`. `bdg dom eval` failed with "Session target not found" in the same session, so use `Runtime.evaluate`.
158: - **Pass 2, state by state:**
159:   1. Enable the domains once per session: `bdg cdp DOM.enable`, then `bdg cdp CSS.enable`. `CSS.forcePseudoState` needs the CSS domain enabled.
160:   2. Resolve the document with `bdg cdp DOM.getDocument` and use its `root.nodeId` as `<rootId>`. Resolve the element with `bdg cdp DOM.querySelector --params '{"nodeId":<rootId>,"selector":"<css>"}'` and use the result's `nodeId` as `<id>`.
161:   3. Emulate reduced motion first, `bdg cdp Emulation.setEmulatedMedia --params '{"features":[{"name":"prefers-reduced-motion","value":"reduce"}]}'`. A style read straight after forcing a state otherwise returns a mid-transition value.
162:   4. Force each state with its own call, `bdg cdp CSS.forcePseudoState --params '{"nodeId":<id>,"forcedPseudoClasses":["hover"]}'`, then `["active"]` and `["focus"]`. Force `focus-visible` only when `bdg cdp --describe CSS.forcePseudoState` confirms support. Clear with an empty `forcedPseudoClasses` list before the next state.
163:   5. The disabled state comes from the element's `disabled` attribute, not a forced class.
164:   6. Capture each state with `bdg dom screenshot <path>`, and confirm the capture shows the state.
165:   7. Check dark mode with the same `setEmulatedMedia` method and `{"name":"prefers-color-scheme","value":"dark"}`, only where the project supports dark mode. Reset with `--params '{"features":[]}'`.
166:   8. If CDP cannot run, use real hover, click and keyboard focus. If neither path runs, record `NOT RUN` with the reason.
167: - **Pass 5, range and access:**
168:   1. Test narrow, medium and wide widths below and above W with `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`. Reset with `bdg cdp Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride`.
169:   2. Check 200 percent zoom with `bdg cdp Emulation.setPageScaleFactor --params '{"pageScaleFactor":2}'`, and reset with `1`.
170:   3. Traverse the page with real Tab presses, and record the focus order and any trap.
171:   4. Check names, roles and states with `bdg cdp Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, or with a manual screen-reader pass.
172:   5. Read computed text and background colours with `Runtime.evaluate` as above, then check contrast against the target `sk-design-fundamentals` sets.
173:   6. Record any check that cannot run as `NOT RUN` with the reason.
174: - Use [mcp-aside-devtools](../../../mcp-tooling/mcp-aside-devtools/SKILL.md) as the fallback renderer. Its `aside repl` is Playwright-compatible and can capture screenshots, but it has no CDP-domain parity, so it cannot force states or emulate media. Keep `bdg` for those checks.
175: 
176: See [mcp-chrome-devtools](../../../mcp-tooling/mcp-chrome-devtools/SKILL.md) for documented `bdg` commands.
177: 
178: ### Verdict and Report
179: 
180: The overall result is `PASS` only when every pass passes. Record a pass that cannot run as `NOT RUN` with its reason, and the overall verdict is then `INCOMPLETE`, never `PASS`.
181: 
182: The report names:
183: 
184: - The frame, node id and W.
185: - The installed token package and version, and the tool used for each pass.
186: - Capture paths, the state matrix, the rendered value table and the variable-to-token table.
187: - The lag list and overall verdict.
188: 
189: ---
190: 
191: ## 6. RED FLAGS
192: 
193: Stop and restructure when the code shows any of these:
194: 
195: - Most children are absolutely positioned.
196: - A literal frame width such as `375px` or `width: 375`.
197: - A fixed height on a container that holds text.
198: - Wrapper depth that mirrors the Figma layer panel.
199: - Pixel or hex literals pasted from the inspect panel.
200: - One component per Figma variant instead of one component with props.
201: - Class names copied from layer names, such as `.frame-427` or `.auto-layout-wrapper`.

14: # Frontend Practice
15: 
16: Shared rules for frontend work, expressed through the web layer and the project-specific layer.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: This file owns the shared principles. The core states what good frontend work must preserve.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: - Checking a change against the eleven principles
29: - Deciding values and precedence
30: - Reading a Figma frame as a reference
31: - Declaring a project mode override
32: - Running the frontend pre-completion checklist
33: 
34: ### Boundaries
35: 
36: This file does not own:
37: 
38: - **Web mechanics.** The web layer expresses the principles through DOM and CSS. It names the vocabulary and mechanics that implement them, in [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
39: - **Project-specific conventions.** Each project mode adds the conventions it uses, in its own `SKILL.md`.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 2. THE ELEVEN PRINCIPLES
44: 
45: 1. **Actions are buttons, and navigation is links.** People get the expected interaction and navigation behavior. See [web structure](web-markup-and-css.md#2-structure-and-semantics).
46: 2. **Every control has a name, a role and a state.** People need to identify a control and understand its current condition. See [web structure](web-markup-and-css.md#2-structure-and-semantics).
47: 3. **Every input has a visible label, and its affordance matches the data.** A visible label stays available after a person starts typing, while the input cue helps them enter the right data. See [web forms](web-markup-and-css.md#3-forms).
48: 4. **Layout follows content flow, siblings have consistent spacing, text containers grow with their text, overlays leave the flow, and content respects device safe areas.** This lets content adapt without clipping or hiding ordinary content. See [web layout](web-markup-and-css.md#4-layout).
49: 5. **Text survives translation and font scaling.** Longer translations and larger system text must remain readable and reachable. See [web responsive rules](web-markup-and-css.md#5-responsive).
50: 6. **Every image has a text-alternative decision and reserved dimensions.** People using assistive technology need the image's meaning, and the layout needs its space before it loads. See [web media](web-markup-and-css.md#6-media).
51: 7. **Values come from installed tokens, and a missing token is reported.** Installed tokens keep values consistent across the app, while a report gives the design system a clear gap to resolve. See [web CSS architecture](web-markup-and-css.md#7-css-architecture).
52: 8. **Figma is a reference, not a code structure.** A design shows intended appearance and states, while the app's own conventions decide its structure. See the [web boundary](web-markup-and-css.md#1-overview) and [Figma to code](figma-to-code.md).
53: 9. **Responsive behavior is checked at narrow, medium and wide widths and under zoom.** These checks expose wrapping, overflow and clipping before release. See [web responsive rules](web-markup-and-css.md#5-responsive).
54: 10. **Assistive-technology checks are part of completion, and non-essential motion respects the user's reduced-motion setting.** They confirm names, order, states and feedback when people do not use the visual layout. See the [web checklist](web-markup-and-css.md#9-pre-completion-checklist).
55: 11. **Text and controls meet the contrast target set by sk-design-fundamentals on every theme the mode supports.** Contrast remains readable in each supported theme. See [web structure](web-markup-and-css.md#2-structure-and-semantics) and [sk-design-fundamentals](../../../sk-design/sk-design-fundamentals/SKILL.md).
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 3. VALUES AND PRECEDENCE
60: 
61: Values come from the project's installed tokens. Report a missing token instead of inventing a value. When the tokens or the frame leave a value open, use [sk-design-fundamentals](../../../sk-design/sk-design-fundamentals/SKILL.md) for guidance.
62: 
63: Use [interaction-craft.md](../../../sk-design/sk-design-fundamentals/references/interaction-craft.md) for interaction detail. This core carries only the shared interaction rules:
64: 
65: - Make thumb-operated targets 44 px. Keep 32 px as the dense floor.
66: - Keep font weight stable across interaction states.
67: - Update optimistically, then roll back when the server reports an error.
68: - Show feedback beside the action that triggered it.
69: - Design empty states with a useful next action.
70: 
71: ---
72: 
73: ## 4. FIGMA AS REFERENCE
74: 
75: A Figma frame records intended appearance and states. Its layer tree does not decide the code structure. The five-pass check is in [figma-to-code.md Section 5](figma-to-code.md#5-the-check).
76: 
77: 1. **Passes:** same-width comparison, state by state, render and source token checks, variable to token, range and access.
78: 2. **Verdict:** PASS only when all passes pass. A pass marked NOT RUN with its reason makes the overall verdict INCOMPLETE.
79: 3. **Figma transport ladder:** use an available official Figma connection first, then a verified connector or CLI, then a static export marked as possibly stale.
80: 
81: Check dark mode only where the mode supports it.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## 5. OVERRIDES
86: 
87: A project mode wins for its app when it declares a change to one core or web-layer statement. A mode may replace, extend or disable that statement. It records each change under a Frontend overrides heading in its own SKILL.md, naming the section, action and reason. When nothing differs, the heading says: none: this mode follows the core and its web layer unchanged. A project mode's completion report names the overrides it applied.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## 6. LAYERS AND TOPIC FILES
92: 
93: Load this core, the web layer and the one topic file the change touches. Load a second topic file only when the change crosses into it.
94: 
95: **Layers**
96: 
97: | Layer | Applies to | Reference |
98: |---|---|---|
99: | Web | Any DOM and CSS app, whatever the framework | [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md) |
100: | Project-specific | Each project's own conventions | The project mode's `SKILL.md` |
101: 
102: **Web topic files**
103: 
104: | Topic | File | Load when |
105: |---|---|---|
106: | Elements and attributes | [web-elements-and-attributes.md](web-elements-and-attributes.md) | Adding or changing a dialog, popover, disclosure, form-control attribute or resource hint |
107: | Cascade and selectors | [web-cascade-and-selectors.md](web-cascade-and-selectors.md) | Changing selector reach, cascade layers, specificity or component style boundaries |
108: | Layout and sizing | [web-layout-and-sizing.md](web-layout-and-sizing.md) | Changing stacking, containing blocks, intrinsic sizing, container queries or scrolling |
109: | Accessibility patterns | [web-accessibility-patterns.md](web-accessibility-patterns.md) | Changing a widget pattern, accessible name, focus behavior, live region, browser preference or form validation and error messaging |
110: | Performance and loading | [web-performance-and-loading.md](web-performance-and-loading.md) | Changing vitals, resource loading, image delivery, fonts or main-thread work |
111: | Internationalization | [web-internationalization.md](web-internationalization.md) | Changing locale, direction, bidirectional text, formatting or translation tolerance |
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 7. PRE-COMPLETION CHECKLIST
116: 
117: - [ ] Actions use button behavior, navigation uses link behavior, and every control has a name, role and state.
118: - [ ] Every input has a visible label and matching affordance, and text remains readable after translation and font scaling.
119: - [ ] Layout follows content flow, respects safe areas and is checked at narrow, medium and wide widths and under zoom.
120: - [ ] Every image has a text alternative and reserved dimensions, and values use installed tokens with missing tokens reported.
121: - [ ] Figma informs appearance and states without dictating code structure, and the verdict is PASS or explains why it is INCOMPLETE.
122: - [ ] Non-essential motion respects the user's reduced-motion setting, and assistive-technology checks are recorded.
123: - [ ] Text and controls meet the contrast target on supported themes, and dark mode is checked only where the mode supports it.

37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. CASCADE AND SPECIFICITY
40: 
41: ### CS1. Cascade decision order
42: 
43: - **Rule:** Resolve competing declarations by origin and importance, layer order, specificity, scope proximity when scoped rules apply, then source order.
44: - **Why:** The cascade compares these criteria in order, so a later rule cannot win by source order when an earlier criterion already decided the result.
45: - **When not to:** Skip the comparison when the declarations do not apply to the same element and property.
46: - **Pitfall:** Normal unlayered declarations outrank normal declarations in named layers, while important declarations reverse layer precedence.
47: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
48: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS cascade](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Cascade)
49: 
50: ### CS2. Global cascade layer order
51: 
52: - **Rule:** Declare the cascade layer order once in a global stylesheet before component styles load.
53: - **Why:** Layer order is established the first time each layer name appears. Component style injection can vary with load order, so per-component layer blocks cannot define a reliable shared order.
54: - **When not to:** Use unlayered styles only when the app deliberately relies on the unlayered precedence boundary.
55: - **Pitfall:** A deeply scoped rule inside a layer loses to an unlayered rule even when its selector looks stronger.
56: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `cascade-layers`). Chrome 99 / Firefox 97 / Safari 15.4.
57: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS cascade layers (@layer)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@layer)
58: 
59: ### CS3. Specificity arithmetic
60: 
61: - **Rule:** Count IDs, class-like selectors and type selectors in separate specificity columns before changing a selector.
62: - **Why:** IDs add to the first column, classes, attributes and pseudo-classes add to the second, and type selectors and pseudo-elements add to the third. A component-scoping attribute such as `[data-scope]` adds one class-like unit.
63: - **When not to:** Do not raise specificity when the actual conflict comes from origin, importance or cascade layer order.
64: - **Pitfall:** A selector such as `.card[data-scope]` has specificity `0-2-0`, not `0-1-0`.
65: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
66: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS specificity](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Specificity)
67: 
68: ---
69:

71: 
72: ### CS4. Zero-specificity and maximum-argument selectors
73: 
74: - **Rule:** Wrap low-priority defaults in `:where()` and use `:is()` when the matching alternatives should share the strongest argument's specificity.
75: - **Why:** `:where()` contributes zero specificity, while `:is()` contributes the specificity of its most specific argument.
76: - **When not to:** Keep a direct class selector when the alternatives would obscure which component states match.
77: - **Pitfall:** Adding a high-specificity selector to one `:is()` alternative raises the specificity of the entire selector.

79: - **See also:** [MDN: :is()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:is)
80: 
81: ### CS5. Narrow relational matching with :has()
82: 
83: - **Rule:** Keep `:has()` selectors narrow and close to the component that owns the matching relationship.
84: - **Why:** The browser reevaluates relational matches as the relevant DOM changes, and a broad ancestor selector can increase style invalidation work.
85: - **When not to:** Prefer an existing direct selector when the relationship is already represented by a simple parent or sibling structure.
86: - **Pitfall:** A broad rule such as `body:has(.is-open)` makes unrelated subtree changes relevant to a page-level selector.
87: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2026-06-19 (web-features `has`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 121 / Safari 15.4.
88: - **See also:** [MDN: :has()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:has)
89: 
90: ---
91: 
92: ## 4. NESTING, SCOPE AND PROPERTIES
93: 
94: ### CS6. Native nesting and the nesting selector
95: 
96: - **Rule:** Use `&` to make the parent selector explicit inside native CSS nesting.
97: - **Why:** The nesting selector represents the full parent selector, so `&:hover` and `.theme &` express relationships without Sass-style string concatenation.
98: - **When not to:** Keep a selector flat when nesting would hide its reach or increase selector complexity.
99: - **Pitfall:** `&-active` does not append a suffix to a class name as it would in Sass.
100: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2026-06-11 (web-features `nesting`). Chrome 120 / Firefox 117 / Safari 17.2.
101: - **See also:** [MDN: Using CSS nesting](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_nesting/Using_CSS_nesting)
102: 
103: ### CS7. Scoped selector boundaries
104: 
105: - **Rule:** Use `@scope` to limit a rule to a component subtree when the required browsers support it.
106: - **Why:** Scoped rules stop at the declared scope boundary, and scope proximity breaks a tie after specificity without changing the selector's specificity.
107: - **When not to:** Use the established component scoping mechanism when a target browser does not support `@scope`.
108: - **Pitfall:** A scope boundary does not prevent unscoped rules from matching the same descendants. In Safari 26.0 through 26.3, rules inside `@scope` do not apply to `<input>` and `<textarea>`; support is complete from 26.4.
109: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2026-03-24 (web-features `scope`). Chrome 143 / Firefox 146 / Safari 26.4.
110: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS @scope](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@scope)
111: 
112: ### CS8. Registered custom properties
113: 
114: - **Rule:** Register a custom property with `@property` when its type, inheritance behavior or animation behavior must be explicit.
115: - **Why:** Registration gives the browser a syntax, an `inherits` setting and an initial value, which lets typed values interpolate during animation.
116: - **When not to:** Keep an unregistered property when it only carries an inherited token and needs no typed animation.
117: - **Pitfall:** A registered property with the wrong `inherits` value can stop a theme token from reaching its descendants.
118: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-07-09 (web-features `registered-custom-properties`). Chrome 85 / Firefox 128 / Safari 16.4.
119: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS @property](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@property)
120:

122:

126: - **Pitfall:** A store-owned `.is-open` class can drift from the expanded state already present on the control.
127: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
128: - **See also:** [MDN: Attribute selectors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Attribute_selectors)

13: # Web Accessibility Patterns
14: 
15: Widget contracts, focus handling and browser accessibility preferences for web interfaces.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: This file covers widget behavior, focus and browser accessibility preferences. Support summaries use the web-features Baseline classifications and browser-version data.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Adding or changing a modal dialog
28: - Mapping a component library's behavior to a widget pattern
29: - Naming controls or moving focus
30: - Adding announcements or honoring browser accessibility preferences
31: - Building a widget pattern or wiring form validation and error messages
32: 
33: ### Boundaries
34: 
35: - Native element choice and baseline semantics: [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
36: - State selectors such as `:focus-visible`: [web-cascade-and-selectors.md](web-cascade-and-selectors.md).
37: - Element and attribute mechanics for dialogs, popovers and forms: [web-elements-and-attributes.md](web-elements-and-attributes.md).
38: 
39: ---
40: 
41: ## 2. MODAL DIALOG CONTRACT
42: 
43: ### A1. Modal dialog
44: 
45: - **Rule:** Use native `<dialog>` with `showModal()` or a component library's documented modal behavior.
46: - **Why:** These mechanisms provide top-layer placement, Escape handling, focus containment and an inert background.
47: - **When not to:** Use a non-modal dialog when the surrounding page must remain interactive.
48: - **Pitfall:** Setting `aria-modal="true"` on an ordinary element hides the rest of the page from assistive technology without making the page inert.
49: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `dialog`). Chrome 37 / Firefox 98 / Safari 15.4.
50: - **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Dialog (modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 3. LIBRARY MAPPING
55: 
56: | Pattern | Integration boundary |
57: |---|---|
58: | Modal dialog | Close through the dialog lifecycle so focus returns to the opener. |
59: | Menu button | Use a disclosure and navigation list for site navigation; a menu role promises menu keyboard behavior. |
60: | Tabs, listbox or combobox | Do not add tabindex values or arrow-key handlers when a component manages roving focus; treat its autocomplete as a combobox and do not redeclare supplied roles. |
61: | Accordion, disclosure or tooltip | Keep expanded state aligned; disabled controls may not receive focus, and a tooltip cannot be the only label. |
62: | Status region, table or grid | Keep the live region mounted before changing its text; set `aria-sort` on the sorted header when needed. |
63: | Focus styling | Keep a visible replacement if an outline is removed. |
64: 
65: When a component library provides widget roles, state, focus movement or announcements, use that behavior as the source of truth. For hand-written widgets, implement the complete pattern described below.
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 4. NAMES AND FOCUS
70: 
71: ### A2. Accessible name order
72: 
73: - **Rule:** Prefer `aria-labelledby` that points to visible text, and preserve the order `aria-labelledby`, `aria-label`, host-language label, then `title`.
74: - **Why:** A higher-priority naming source replaces lower-priority sources in the computed accessible name.
75: - **When not to:** Omit ARIA naming attributes when a native label already provides the intended name.
76: - **Pitfall:** An `aria-label` of `Send` replaces visible `Submit` text and can break speech input that uses the visible label.
77: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
78: - **See also:** [MDN: Accessible name calculation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Guides/Accessible_name_calculation)
79: 
80: ### A3. Roving tabindex and active descendant
81: 
82: - **Rule:** Use roving tabindex for items that move DOM focus, and use `aria-activedescendant` when focus stays on a text input.
83: - **Why:** Roving tabindex moves browser focus, while `aria-activedescendant` exposes an active child without moving focus from its owner.
84: - **When not to:** Use neither pattern for ordinary links or buttons that already provide the needed keyboard behavior.
85: - **Pitfall:** The active descendant must reference a rendered element with a stable ID, so virtualized options can leave a dangling reference.
86: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
87: - **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/)
88: 
89: ### A4. Focus return through the dialog reference
90: 
91: - **Rule:** Close a library-managed overlay through its documented lifecycle so it can restore focus to the opener.
92: - **Why:** The component lifecycle can return focus after the modal leaves the top layer.
93: - **When not to:** Focus a logical successor when the opener no longer exists after the interaction.
94: - **Pitfall:** Removing a dialog through application state can bypass the component lifecycle and leave focus on `body`.
95: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
96: - **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Dialog (modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)
97: 
98: ### A5. Focus-visible styling
99: 
100: - **Rule:** Use `:focus-visible` for browser-selected focus styling and retain a clear keyboard focus indicator.
101: - **Why:** The browser tracks input modality and matches the selector when it determines a focus indicator is needed. Use [CS9](web-cascade-and-selectors.md#cs9-existing-state-selector-contract) for the state-selector contract that applies to focus styling.
102: - **When not to:** Add an explicit focus state when a programmatic focus change must always display a ring.
103: - **Pitfall:** Programmatic focus may not match `:focus-visible`, even when the newly focused container needs an indicator.
104: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `focus-visible`). Chrome 86 / Firefox 85 / Safari 15.4.
105: - **See also:** [MDN: :focus-visible](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:focus-visible)
106: 
107: ### A6. Inert background
108: 
109: - **Rule:** Set `inert` on the background while a custom modal is open, and leave the modal subtree interactive.
110: - **Why:** Inert removes descendants from sequential focus and interaction, while `aria-hidden` only changes the accessibility tree.
111: - **When not to:** Do not set `inert` when the surface is a non-modal overlay that leaves the page usable.
112: - **Pitfall:** Applying `inert` to the overlay itself makes its controls unreachable.
113: - **Support:** See [EA4](web-elements-and-attributes.md#ea4-inert-background-boundary) for browser support.
114: - **See also:** [MDN: inert global attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/inert)
115: 
116: ---
117: 
118: ## 5. ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PREFERENCES
119: 
120: ### A7. Live-region timing
121: 
122: - **Rule:** Mount a live-region container before updating its text, set `aria-atomic="true"` when the whole message must be read and reserve assertive announcements for interrupting errors.
123: - **Why:** Assistive technology observes changes to an existing live region and may miss a region created with its first message.
124: - **When not to:** Do not add a live region to content already announced through ordinary navigation or focus movement.
125: - **Pitfall:** Recreating an alert region for each render can repeat the same message or fail to announce it.
126: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
127: - **See also:** [MDN: aria-live](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-live)
128: 
129: ### A8. Forced colors
130: 
131: - **Rule:** Use system colors such as `Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `Highlight` and `HighlightText` for essential text, and use borders rather than shadows for boundaries in forced-colors mode.
132: - **Why:** The browser can replace author colors and remove background images when forced colors are active.
133: - **When not to:** Use `forced-color-adjust: none` only when preserving a specific color is necessary to convey meaning.
134: - **Pitfall:** Hard-coded SVG fills and shadow-only borders can disappear from the high-contrast presentation.
135: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-03-12 (web-features `forced-colors`). Chrome 89 / Firefox 89 / Safari 16.
136: - **See also:** [MDN: forced-colors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors)
137: 
138: ### A9. Reduced motion
139: 
140: - **Rule:** Put optional motion inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` and keep progress feedback available in both modes.
141: - **Why:** The default path remains safe when the preference is unknown or reduced, while the opt-in applies motion only to users who allow it.
142: - **When not to:** Do not add an animation when a state change is already clear without motion.
143: - **Pitfall:** A global animation reset can remove a loading spinner and leave no visible progress cue.
144: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `prefers-reduced-motion`). Chrome 74 / Firefox 63 / Safari 10.1.
145: - **See also:** [MDN: prefers-reduced-motion](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion)
146: 
147: ### A10. Contrast, color scheme and transparency preferences
148: 
149: - **Rule:** Set `color-scheme` for supported themes, honor contrast preferences, and treat reduced-transparency styling as a feature-detected enhancement over an opaque baseline.
150: - **Why:** The media preferences expose user display choices, while `color-scheme` lets browser controls adapt to the declared theme.
151: - **When not to:** Keep the opaque baseline when the interface has no transparency effect to reduce.
152: - **Pitfall:** Depending on `prefers-reduced-transparency` alone leaves Safari users without the fallback, and Firefox support requires a preference flag.
153: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-11-30 (web-features `prefers-contrast`). Chrome 96 / Firefox 101 / Safari 14.1. Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `prefers-color-scheme`). Chrome 76 / Firefox 67 / Safari 12.1. Baseline widely available since 2024-08-03 (web-features `color-scheme`). Chrome 98 / Firefox 96 / Safari 13. Baseline limited availability (web-features `prefers-reduced-transparency`). Chrome 119 / Firefox unsupported / Safari unsupported.
154: - **See also:** [MDN: prefers-contrast](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-contrast)
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## 6. WIDGET PATTERNS
159: 
160: ### A11. Carousel
161: 
162: - **Rule:** Provide a visible rotation control, pause rotation on hover and focus and set `aria-live="off"` while it rotates.
163: - **Why:** Rotation changes content without user input, so a pause control and controlled announcements preserve predictable navigation.
164: - **When not to:** Omit rotation controls when the carousel never rotates automatically.
165: - **Pitfall:** Previous and next buttons without labels leave their direction unclear to screen-reader users.
166: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
167: - **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Carousel](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/)
168: 
169: ### A12. Table and grid
170: 
171: - **Rule:** Use a native table for static data and use `role="grid"` only when the widget implements its full keyboard interaction model.
172: - **Why:** A grid role promises managed focus and keyboard navigation beyond a table's row and column relationships.
173: - **When not to:** Use a grid when users edit, select or navigate cells as an interactive widget.
174: - **Pitfall:** A sortable table needs `aria-sort` on the currently sorted header.
175: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
176: - **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Grid](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/)
177: 
178: ### A13. Menu button
179: 
180: - **Rule:** Pair `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded` with Up or Down to open, Home and End, typeahead, Escape to close and return focus and Tab to close.
181: - **Why:** The menu-button pattern exposes a popup menu whose items use composite-widget keyboard behavior.
182: - **When not to:** Use a disclosure button and navigation list for site navigation.
183: - **Pitfall:** Applying `role="menu"` to ordinary site navigation changes assistive-technology expectations without supplying menu keyboard behavior.
184: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
185: - **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Menu button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/)
186: 
187: ### A14. Tooltip
188: 
189: - **Rule:** Give supplemental content `role="tooltip"`, associate its trigger through `aria-describedby`, show it on hover and focus and let Escape dismiss it.
190: - **Why:** The described-by relationship makes the tooltip's supplemental text available when the trigger receives focus.
191: - **When not to:** Use a dialog or popover when the content contains interactive controls.
192: - **Pitfall:** A tooltip on a disabled control may never appear, and a tooltip cannot provide the control's only name.
193: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
194: - **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Tooltip](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/)
195: 
196: ---
197: 
198: ## 7. FORMS AND VALIDATION
199: 
200: ### A15. Framework validation layers
201: 
202: - **Rule:** For forms handled by a framework validation layer, render app feedback and confirm whether the framework disables native browser validation. Keep native constraint attributes so the framework can read them.
203: - **Why:** A framework may add `novalidate` or otherwise replace browser validation bubbles while still using attributes such as `required` and `min` as validator inputs.
204: - **When not to:** Use browser-native validation when its message UI is the intended path.
205: - **Pitfall:** `setCustomValidity()` does not restore browser validation UI while `novalidate` remains on the form.
206: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
207: - **See also:** [MDN: Constraint validation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Constraint_validation)
208: 
209: ### A16. Error association in library and hand-written fields
210: 
211: - **Rule:** Inside a component library's form-field wrapper, let the library associate its error and hint messages. In a hand-written field, bind the visible message ID and invalid state to the control.
212: - **Why:** A library may add message IDs to the input's `aria-describedby` list and update its `aria-invalid` state. For a hand-written field, give each message an ID, reference it from the control and set the invalid state when validation fails.
213: - **When not to:** Do not add a duplicate `aria-describedby` ID or invalid-state binding when the component already manages both.
214: - **Pitfall:** A library may show an error when a control is invalid and touched or when the form is submitted. A hand-written component that shows errors only when dirty behaves differently.
215: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
216: - **See also:** [WAI: Forms tutorial, notifications](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/)
217: 
218: ### A17. Error summary and focus on submit
219: 
220: - **Rule:** After a failed submit, focus the first invalid control or an error summary that links to each invalid control.
221: - **Why:** The summary gives assistive technology users one place to review errors and jump to the affected fields.
222: - **When not to:** A single-field form, such as a search box, can keep focus on its field and show the inline error there.
223: - **Pitfall:** After a submit handler marks every control as touched, focus remains on the submit button unless code moves it. Newly rendered error text is not automatically announced.
224: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
225: - **See also:** [WAI: Forms tutorial, notifications](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/)
226: 
227: ### A18. Async validator pending state
228: 
229: - **Rule:** Block submission while a form is pending as well as when it is invalid. Expose validation progress with `aria-busy` on the field group or a polite status message.
230: - **Why:** An asynchronous validator can leave a form pending while both its valid and invalid states are false.
231: - **When not to:** A form with no async validators needs only the `invalid` check.
232: - **Pitfall:** A submit check that reads only `form.invalid` can run before async validation finishes. A disabled control leaves the tab order and is excluded from the form's aggregate value.
233: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
234: - **See also:** [MDN: Constraint validation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Constraint_validation)

13: # Web Accessibility Patterns
14: 
15: Widget contracts, focus handling and browser accessibility preferences for web interfaces.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: This file covers widget behavior, focus and browser accessibility preferences. Support summaries use the web-features Baseline classifications and browser-version data.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Adding or changing a modal dialog
28: - Mapping a component library's behavior to a widget pattern
29: - Naming controls or moving focus
30: - Adding announcements or honoring browser accessibility preferences
31: - Building a widget pattern or wiring form validation and error messages
32: 
33: ### Boundaries
34: 
35: - Native element choice and baseline semantics: [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
36: - State selectors such as `:focus-visible`: [web-cascade-and-selectors.md](web-cascade-and-selectors.md).
37: - Element and attribute mechanics for dialogs, popovers and forms: [web-elements-and-attributes.md](web-elements-and-attributes.md).
38: 
39: ---
40: 
41: ## 2. MODAL DIALOG CONTRACT
42: 
43: ### A1. Modal dialog
44: 
45: - **Rule:** Use native `<dialog>` with `showModal()` or a component library's documented modal behavior.
46: - **Why:** These mechanisms provide top-layer placement, Escape handling, focus containment and an inert background.
47: - **When not to:** Use a non-modal dialog when the surrounding page must remain interactive.
48: - **Pitfall:** Setting `aria-modal="true"` on an ordinary element hides the rest of the page from assistive technology without making the page inert.
49: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `dialog`). Chrome 37 / Firefox 98 / Safari 15.4.
50: - **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Dialog (modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 3. LIBRARY MAPPING
55: 
56: | Pattern | Integration boundary |
57: |---|---|
58: | Modal dialog | Close through the dialog lifecycle so focus returns to the opener. |
59: | Menu button | Use a disclosure and navigation list for site navigation; a menu role promises menu keyboard behavior. |
60: | Tabs, listbox or combobox | Do not add tabindex values or arrow-key handlers when a component manages roving focus; treat its autocomplete as a combobox and do not redeclare supplied roles. |
61: | Accordion, disclosure or tooltip | Keep expanded state aligned; disabled controls may not receive focus, and a tooltip cannot be the only label. |
62: | Status region, table or grid | Keep the live region mounted before changing its text; set `aria-sort` on the sorted header when needed. |
63: | Focus styling | Keep a visible replacement if an outline is removed. |
64: 
65: When a component library provides widget roles, state, focus movement or announcements, use that behavior as the source of truth. For hand-written widgets, implement the complete pattern described below.
66: 
67: ---
68:

71: ### A2. Accessible name order

196: ---
197: 
198: ## 7. FORMS AND VALIDATION

200: ### A15. Framework validation layers

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]

708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073:

26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
